blocks.content: Biodiversity follows a latitudinal gradient — diversity increases from the poles toward the equator.
• Tropical rainforests contain over half of the world's species.
• Coral reefs are known as the 'rainforests of the sea'.
• Islands exhibit high endemism but are highly vulnerable.
• Mountain regions show altitudinal zonation of species.

rows: Relatively undisturbed for millions of years
Subjected to frequent glaciations in the past
Maximum solar energy and higher productivity
Lower solar energy input and productivity
High species diversity and niche specialisation

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Tropical regions have remained relatively undisturbed by glaciations for millions of years, allowing uninterrupted evolutionary diversification.
Tropical environments are less seasonal, more constant, and predictable, which fosters high niche specialisation.
Higher availability of solar energy in the tropics directly contributes to greater productivity and species richness.

blocks.content: • Stable climate over millions of years.

items: Competitive exams frequently test the three main factors behind tropical biodiversity: evolutionary time, environmental constancy, and solar productivity.
Understand the difference between tropical stability and temperate glaciation cycles as a driver for speciation.
Remember that niche specialisation is significantly higher in predictable tropical climates.

blocks.content: • High solar energy leading to greater primary productivity.
